text:
maria: heads up — p95 for /v1/embeddings on io-034 spiked from ~12ms to 120ms at 11:20 UTC, and we see a simultaneous drop in kv prefix hit-rate

josh: noticed it too, perf dashboards show prefix_hitrate going from 78% -> 4% over 3m :eyes:

kai: running live profile now, attaching quick flame snapshot (s3 link)

sandeep: eviction rate on shard io-034 jumped to 2.3k/s right at 11:19. top evicted prefixes are almost all from tenant:acme-batch-seeder

anya: oh — we rolled PR #5321 (kv seeding/priming change) yesterday that enabled background prefill for long-running jobs, pinging infra owners

maria: can we confirm correlation with PR? timeline: deploy 02:15 UTC yesterday, small steady traffic, then batch job kicked off at 11:17 UTC and then collapse

josh: extracting logs:
```
kv.eviction_rate{shard="io-034"} 2300 161000.68
kv.prefix_cardinality{shard="io-034"} 3_180_122 -> 3_980_212
kv.prefix_hitrate 0.04
```

kai: profile shows lots of kernel fallback churn during requests that hit cache miss — fallback to cpu-bound kernel for small batch sizes, CPU steal up 60% on p99 workers

sandeep: root cause hypothesis: the seeding job created a huge number of near-unique prefixes, polluting LRU windows. eviction + kernel fallback => increased latency and more misses => positive feedback loop :boom:

anya: deploy-bot: canary deploy v2 completed for cluster io-0x at 02:15 UTC (reaction :rocket:)

maria: immediate mitigation: 1) pause the seeder job 2) bump kv.max_prefix_entries for noisy tenants? 3) roll back prefill flag in PR 5321 if we can

josh: paused the job at 11:28 UTC — prefix_hitrate started recovering slowly (4% -> 22% in 6m). eviction rate dropped to 430/s

kai: flipping the kernel selection fallback threshold to prefer stable small-batch kernels for these shards reduced p95 from 120ms -> 28ms in the canary group

sandeep: we should also add a guard: if a single tenant creates >100k new prefixes in 5m, throttle seeding or route to dedicated pool. I'll file a ticket

anya: filed RN: INF-847 — guardrail for prefix bursts + alerting for sudden prefix_cardinal growth. assign to sandeep

maria: next steps: revert the automatic prefill by default and move that to opt-in for now. postmortem notes: checkpoint eviction policy assumptions, add synthetic test that exercises seeding at scale in staging

josh: quick commands to validate (run on prod-metrics):
```
# check top evicting tenants
promql: topk(20, sum by(tenant) (rate(kv.eviction_events_total[1m])))
# prefix growth
promql: increase(kv.prefix_keys_created_total[5m])
```

kai: also add a tracing tag on prefix-priming jobs so we can correlate easily next time

maria: thanks all — keeping thread open for remediation steps and postmortem draft. anyone else seeing residual pain?

josh: p95 back to ~30ms on io-034, will watch 24h. closing mitigation loop once RN deployed and PR reverted

sandeep: I'll schedule a follow-up to discuss safer seeding algorithms (probabilistic sampling + cap per-tenant)

anya: adding postmortem owners: maria, josh, sandeep. ETA for draft EOD tomorrow

deploy-bot: rollback of feature flag kv.prefill.enabled -> false scheduled and applied at 11:46 UTC (run-id: run-7729) :white_check_mark:
